Leather, Tanning Materials and Allied Products Sectional Committee, CHD 17 


FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Leather, Tanning Materials and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Chemical Division Council. 


Slickers are used in leather industry for setting operation to have a final flat, smooth leather free from wrinkles, 
fold mark, and drawn grain. Until recently these slickers were being fabricated by the tanners themselves 
according to their individual requirements. This standard is intended to guide the manufacturer to produce slickers 
to suit the need of the tanner in general. 


The slicker consists of a wooden handle and a blade which is inserted in a slot of the handle. The blades may be 
of brass, glass, stone, stainless steel or of any other material which does not cause stains to the leather during use. 
The general pattern of different slickers used in the trade at present is more or less the same and varies in respect 
of the type of the blade used. In view of this, rationalization of existing designs has been recommended in this 
standard to a large extent without disturbing much, the current trade practices. 


This standard was originally published in 1970. The Committee felt a need to revise the standard with a view 
to update the standard based on the experience of last five decades and on the currently available data. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 5712 : 2023 


Indian Standard 
SLICKERS FOR LEATHER INDUSTRY — SPECIFICATION 


( First Revision ) 


1SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements, methods 
of sampling and test for slickers used in the leather 
industry for setting leather. 


2 REFERENCES 


The Indian standards listed below contain provisions 
which through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision, and parties to 
agreements based on this Indian standard are 
encouraged to investigate the possibility of 
applying the most recent editions of these 
standards: 


IS No. Title 
IS 2102 General tolerances:

(Part 2) Geometrical tolerances for

indications 
3 TERMINOLOGY 


3.1 Slicker — A contrivance used for setting out 
leather by hand which consists of a blade made of a 
suitable material, such as metal, plastics, stone, 
ebonite or glass embedded in a handle made of 
wood or other suitable material. 


4 TYPE 


Depending upon the material used for the blades of 
the shakers, this standard prescribes five types of 
slickers as follows: 


Type A — Glass slicker; 

Type B — Red stone or Marble slicker; 

Type C — Stainless steel or Nickel silver slicker; 
Type D — Brass slicker; and 

Type E — Rigid PVC or Ebonite slicker. 


5 REQUIREMENTS 


5.1 Materials 

5.1.1 Blades 

The blades of the slickers shall be manufactured 
from either of the following materials, depending on 
the type of the slicker to be produced. 


5.1.1.1 Glass — 5 mm thick 


5.1.1.2 Stone — Red stone or marble stone, cut 
to the thickness of 20 mm. 


5.1.1.3 Stainless steel — minimum 1 mm thickness 
5.1.1.4 Nickel silver — 1 mm thickness minimum 
5.1.1.5 Brass — minimum 2 mm thickness 


5.1.1.6 Rigid PVC or ebonite — minimum 5 mm 
thick 


5.1.2 Handles — Handles of the slicker shall be 
made from the wood which does not stain leather. 


NOTE — Handles manufactured from other suitable 
materials which do not cause stains to leather to break 
during use may be used by agreement between the 
purchaser and the supplier. 


52 Shape and Dimensions 


The shape and dimensions for various types of 
slickers shall be as shown in Fig. 1.

5.3 General Requirements 


5.3.1 The blade and the handle shall be joined with 
suitable pegs, made from wood. 


5.3.2 The blades shall be blunt and evenly smooth 
throughout its working width and shall be free from 
cracks and other manufacturing defects so that no 
scratches are produced in the leather during setting 
operation. The edges shall be rounded smooth. 


5.3.3 The handle shall be finished smooth and a 
French polish or lacquer shall further be applied to 
give a bright finish. 


5.3.4 Dimensions shall be checked by suitable 
calipers. 


6 TEST METHODS 


6.1 The material shall be examined visually 
for all general requirements prescribed in 
5.3. 


6.2 The material shall be checked for the 
requirements given in 5. Dimensions shall be 
checked by suitable calipers. 


7 MARKING 


7.1 Each handle of the slicker or the package or 
both shall be marked legibly with the following 


IS 5712 : 2023 


particulars: 


a) Type of slicker; and 


b) Name of the manufacturer or trade-mark, if 
any. 


Each slicker or the package or both may also be 
marked with Standard Mark. 


7.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the 
products may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


8 PACKING 


Slickers shall be packed as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier so as to ensure that the 
blades are not damaged during packing and transit. 


9 SCALE OF SAMPLING AND CRITERIA 
FOR CONFORMITY 


Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser 
and supplier, the scale of sampling and criteria for 
conformity shall be as prescribed in Annex A. 


IS 5712 : 2023 


ANNEX A 
(Clause 9) 
SCALE OF SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 


A-1 SCALE OF SAMPLING 
A-1.1 Lot 


In any consignment all the slickers of the same type 
and dimensions and manufactured from the same 
material shall constitute a lot. 


A-1.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to 
the requirements of the specification, tests shall be 
carried out for each lot separately. The number 
of slickers to be selected at random for this 
purpose shall be in accordance with col (1) and (2) 
of Table 1. 


Table 1 Scale of Sampling and Permissible 
Number of Defectives 


(Clause A-1.2, A-1.3 and A-2.2) 


SI No. Lot Size Sample Permissible No. 


Size of Defectives 
N n 
a) 2) (3) (4) 
i) Up to 25 5 0 
ii) 26 to 50 7 0 
iii) 51 to 100 10 1 


A-1.3 The slickers shall be selected at random and to 
ensure the randomness of selection, the following 
procedure is recommended for use: 


Starting from any slicker in a lot, count them in one 
order as (1, 2,3,....... ) up to r and so on, where 
r is the integral part of N/n [N being the lot size 
and n the sample size indicated in col (1) and 
col (2) of Table 1]. Every r slicker thus counted 
shall be selected to constitute the sample. 


A-2 NUMBER OF TEST AND CRITERIA FOR 
CONFORMITY 


A-2.1 The slickers selected according to A-1.3 shall 
be tested for requirements specified in 5. Any slicker 
failing to meet the requirements shall be considered 
as defective. 


A-2.2 If the number of defective slickers found in 
the sample is less than or equal to the 
corresponding permissible number of defectives 
given in col (3) of Table 1, then the lot shall be 
declared as conforming to the requirements 
otherwise not.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: CHD 17 (19517).
